analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md (head lines 393-395). It documents a new DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK variable, a new DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS variable, and updated defaults for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE. No source code, authentication, attestation, encryption, or coordinator contract change is in the supplied evidence. The documented knobs are process-local scheduler and prefill tuning, so they do not touch the trust boundaries TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011, or the assets A-001, A-003 or A-016.

The only possible security relevance is availability and resource use (TB-007, T-029). The docs say a prefill chunk above the default stripe raises paged-KV charges, and that malformed, zero or negative values fall back to 512 or 2048. The docs say both new variables are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. That would let an operator with environment control tune them, but the operator already controls their own provider config. Those values also sit behind the existing memory and slot admission checks the docs describe. No bypass of those checks is shown.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 is unaffected. The doc does not change DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE semantics, the TTL, the HMAC naming, or the per-donation gate. Whether the Swift code in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift matches the documented defaults and clamping was not supplied, so any claim about the implementation is unverified. This is documentation drift rather than a demonstrated security regression. Remaining questions concern whether a larger chunk (2048) combined with KV pool sizing could cause memory-admission underestimation. That cannot be assessed from this patch.
